challenge.reasoning:
The reviewer's facts are right, apart from a few line numbers that are off. At this commit libwebp is hard-wired for every non-Cocoa CMake port. There is no USE_WEBP option: it does not appear in WebKitFeatures.cmake or any Options*.cmake, so the old flag was removed, not renamed. That means the doc is wrong to suggest libwebp is simply optional and can be dropped with a switch.

The reviewer's conclusion ("treat it as required, you must turn off USE_SKIA_ENCODERS, which breaks toDataURL") goes too far. Getting rid of WebP takes a few small, contained patches, and PNG/JPEG encoding keeps working:

(1) ZeroG writes its own PlatformZeroG.cmake, so it can leave out `include(platform/ImageDecoders.cmake)` or add a guard there. That drops WEBPImageDecoder.cpp and WebP::demux.
(2) ScalableImageDecoder.cpp only needs a guard around its include and the two-line signature check.
(3) Skia already ships SkWebpEncoder_none.cpp. Building it next to SkPngEncoderImpl.cpp and SkJpegEncoderImpl.cpp drops WebP::mux while USE_SKIA_ENCODERS stays on, so PNG and JPEG canvas encoding are unaffected. This is a patch to Source/ThirdParty/skia/CMakeLists.txt, which is a WebKit-owned file.
(4) libsharpyuv is only pulled in by the Windows port's own options and platform files. ZeroG's own Options file does not have to copy that.

Things the doc and the reviewer both miss:
- MIMETypeRegistry.cpp hard-codes "image/webp" in the supported image types and in the Skia encoding types. Without patching it, WebKit will claim WebP support but fail to decode.

- Even for an app that doesn't use WebP itself, any remote or third-party content that serves WebP images will break.

Correct status: libwebp cannot be excluded without patches, but a downstream ZeroG patch set can exclude it, so this is not a hard requirement. The estimated cost is about 4 small patches. Recommendation: keep libwebp by default and offer an opt-in ZG_USE_WEBP=OFF build profile.

challenge.reasoning:
The doc says GLib (main loop) is replaced by WTF's RunLoopGeneric, which JSCOnly and PlayStation already use (ZeroG.md:69, :82, :473). The checkout supports this as written. RunLoopGeneric exists, depends only on WTF (Lock, Condition, RedBlackTree), and is compiled without GLib by two upstream ports.

The reviewer's Windows point is correct. The PlatformUse.h default picks the Windows message-pump loop on OS(WINDOWS) and the Cocoa loop on macOS. But that is a build-config detail and doesn't make the claim partly false. The doc never says the generic loop is chosen automatically. Also, upstream already has a "generic loop on Windows" setup: OptionsJSCOnly sets USE_GENERIC_EVENT_LOOP=1 / WTF_DEFAULT_EVENT_LOOP=0 on every OS, including WIN32/MSVC, and PlatformJSCOnly.cmake then compiles RunLoopGeneric.cpp inside its WIN32 setup. So the claim is not partial; it is confirmed, with one config requirement. The reviewer's practical advice stands: copy the JSCOnly pattern in OptionsZeroG.cmake and list RunLoopGeneric.cpp in your own Platform cmake file. PlatformWin.cmake hard-codes RunLoopWin.cpp, so that file can't be reused as-is.

A few of the reviewer's line numbers are off. RunLoopGeneric.cpp is at PlatformJSCOnly.cmake:169 (else branch 167-171), not 170-172. The flags are at OptionsJSCOnly.cmake:109-110, not 107-109; lines 106-107 are the GLib branch.

Things the doc misses that affect implementation:
(1) On Windows, pair the generic loop with win/MainThreadWin.cpp, not generic/MainThreadGeneric.cpp, which uses pthread. JSCOnly does exactly this.
(2) WebCore's RunLoopObserver does nothing on builds that are neither CF nor GLib: schedule() is empty and isScheduled() returns false. GTK/WPE rely on the GLib version for rendering-update/commit timing, so ZeroG must schedule rendering updates another way or implement the observer for the generic loop.
(3) RunLoop::EventObserver, used by the inspector's PageTimelineAgent, is GLib-only. Timeline run-loop instrumentation will be missing.
(4) To run inside the host app's loop, there are RunLoop::setWakeUpCallback (per thread, stored on currentSingleton) and RunLoop::cycle(), which runs one Iterate pass. But the callback is called while m_loopLock is held, from any thread, so it must not block (PostMessage, writing to a pipe). Also cycle() does not return the next timer deadline, and repeating timers are rescheduled after firing without calling wakeUp(). A host loop that waits only on the wake-up callback can miss timers. Expect a small patch that exposes the next deadline, or a fallback polling timer.
(5) JSRunLoopTimer and RemoteInspectorSocketEndpoint already have generic-loop paths, so JSC and the remote inspector need no GLib.

claims.claim: Fontconfig/expat replaced by a Skia font manager plus your own fallback table
claims.evidence: The replacement font managers exist (skia/src/ports/SkFontMgr_custom_directory.cpp, _embedded.cpp, _empty.cpp). But WebKit's Skia CMake hard-requires Fontconfig on non-Windows (:4-6, :845-852), and WebCore's Skia font code is hardwired to fontconfig outside Windows and Android (FontCacheSkia.cpp:51,70; SkiaSystemFallbackFontCache.cpp:29-110 with FcPattern and FcFontSort).
claims.implication: Feasible, but it means new platform code (a FontCache::fontManager variant and system fallback) and Skia CMake changes, not just swapping a library.

challenge.reasoning: I tried to prove the reviewer wrong and could not. Skia's custom font managers exist in the tree, so the plan can work. But the upstream Skia CMake build and WebCore's Skia font code both pick fontconfig on every non-Windows, non-Android target, and no build option turns that off. Dropping Fontconfig therefore takes three things, not a library swap: (1) edits to Skia's CMakeLists, (2) a new branch in FontCache::fontManager(), and (3) a replacement for SkiaSystemFallbackFontCache, which is written entirely against the fontconfig API. Two things make the reviewer's verdict even stronger. First, the custom Skia managers don't do per-character fallback at all (onMatchFamilyStyleCharacter returns nullptr), so the doc's "own fallback table" is mandatory, not optional. Second, those managers don't map generic family names like serif, sans-serif or monospace the way fontconfig aliases do. On expat: the doc pairs it with Fontconfig, but in this tree Skia only uses expat for Android and for USE_SKIA_OPENTYPE_SVG. That option defaults to ON in GTK/WPE and fails the configure step without expat. Windows is unaffected: upstream already uses DirectWrite and never touches fontconfig, which matches the doc saying this replacement is for Linux.

claims.claim: libepoxy replaced; Skia loads GL/Vulkan with eglGetProcAddress/vkGetInstanceProcAddr; drivers via dlopen
claims.evidence: Without USE_LIBEPOXY, Skia compiles GrGLMakeNativeInterface_egl.cpp and links either ANGLE::EGL or ${EGL_LIBRARIES} (skia/CMakeLists.txt:856-867). WebCore links ANGLE EGL/GLES, or Epoxy, or `OpenGL::GLES` + `${EGL_LIBRARIES}` (WebCore/CMakeLists.txt:2299-2316). That is a link-time DT_NEEDED on libEGL and libGLESv2, not dlopen. Vulkan is not built in WebKit's Skia CMake at all.
claims.implication: To get the dlopen-only model on Linux, you need an EGL/GLES loader shim (or link ANGLE) and must patch the else branch of WebCore's CMake. Vulkan support means adding Skia sources yourself.

challenge.reasoning:
I tried to prove the reviewer wrong and couldn't. The verdict stays PARTIAL.

What is true: libepoxy can be turned off at build time. Without USE_LIBEPOXY, WebKit's Skia CMake builds Skia's own EGL interface, and that interface does call eglGetProcAddress for extension functions.

What is wrong in the doc:
(1) It is not dlopen-only. The same Skia file takes about 100 core GL/EGL functions (glActiveTexture, glBindBuffer, eglQueryString, ...) as direct link-time symbols through GR_GL_CORE_FUNCTIONS_EACH. CMake links ${EGL_LIBRARIES} into Skia and OpenGL::GLES + ${EGL_LIBRARIES} into WebCore. WebCore's GLDisplay.cpp also calls eglInitialize directly. So the binary gets hard DT_NEEDED entries on libEGL and libGLESv2, and the doc's "drivers via dlopen" model does not hold as written.
(2) Skia does not load Vulkan by itself. The Ganesh Vulkan backend expects the embedder to pass a getProc function (skgpu::VulkanGetProc in VulkanBackendContext::fGetProc). So ZeroG must dlopen libvulkan itself and hand over vkGetInstanceProcAddr. WebKit's Skia CMakeLists.txt also contains no Vulkan sources at all, and the defines are only SK_GL / SK_GANESH. The Vulkan sources and headers are in the checkout but are not built.

The reviewer's evidence is accurate. Two things they left out:
- A dlopen-based alternative already exists in the tree. ANGLE's GL-over-EGL backend loads "libEGL.so.1" at runtime (DisplayEGL::getEGLPath). Building with USE_ANGLE_EGL (today only set for Cocoa and Win) would give dlopen semantics on Linux, at the cost of shipping ANGLE.
- Skia's GrGLMakeAssembledInterface(ctx, getProc) lets ZeroG provide its own getProc that resolves from a dlopen'd handle. That fixes Skia but not WebCore's direct EGL calls.

Also, GTK and WPE both force USE_LIBEPOXY TRUE. The non-epoxy branch ZeroG would rely on is therefore not exercised by any Linux upstream port.

claims.claim: lcms2: remove because Skia handles color spaces
claims.evidence: Removal is feasible, but the stated reason is wrong. USE_LCMS defaults ON (WebKitFeatures.cmake:360) and must be turned off explicitly. WebCore's own decoders do the ICC handling, and only through LCMS (PNGImageDecoder.cpp:404-414 `#if USE(LCMS)` with cmsOpenProfileFromMem; JPEGImageDecoder.cpp:47,79,201). Without it, ImageBackingStoreSkia.cpp:39 always tags frames as SkColorSpace::MakeSRGB(), so embedded ICC profiles are ignored.
claims.implication: Add USE_LCMS=OFF to the flag table. Accept that images with embedded ICC profiles (Display P3 photos, for example) will render with wrong colors. Skia's skcms is not wired into WebCore's decoders.

challenge.reasoning:
I tried to show the reviewer was wrong and couldn't. They are right that lcms2 can be removed, and right that the reason the doc gives is wrong for embedded image ICC profiles. In WebCore, ICC profile handling is behind USE(LCMS), and only six files use that guard. All six are image decoders: PNG, JPEG and JPEG-XL, each a .h and .cpp. Nothing in WebCore's decoders calls skcms, SkCodec, SkColorSpace::MakeICC or any other Skia ICC path. The Skia image backing store always tags decoded frames as sRGB.

One correction to the reviewer: "Skia handles color spaces" is partly true. WebCore does use Skia color spaces for named spaces: CSS/canvas Display-P3 and linear P3 (ColorSpaceSkia.cpp), and video/DMABuf Rec709 or PQ/Rec2020. So the doc's reason holds for CSS colors, canvas and video, and fails only for ICC profiles embedded in images. That keeps the claim at PARTIAL, not REFUTED.

There is no rename or alternate flag. The option is USE_LCMS, defined ON by default in WebKitFeatures.cmake. GTK and WPE turn it ON as PUBLIC; Cocoa and PlayStation turn it OFF. OptionsWin.cmake sets no port default, so it inherits ON, and its find_package block stops configuration with a FATAL_ERROR if lcms2 is missing. A new ZeroG port that sets no value would also inherit ON and would need lcms2 unless it sets USE_LCMS=OFF.

Points the doc misses:
1. Even with LCMS on, WebCore converts embedded profiles only to sRGB (cmsCreate_sRGBProfile, INTENT_RELATIVE_COLORIMETRIC). It never converts to the display profile, so wide-gamut images are always clamped to sRGB.
2. With LCMS off, the pixels are passed through unconverted and tagged as sRGB. Wide-gamut and other non-sRGB tagged images (Display P3 or Adobe RGB photos, for example) show wrong colors, usually desaturated.
3. The JPEG-XL decoder's color-management path is guarded by `USE(LCMS) || USE(CG)`, so it loses color management too.
4. Getting correct ICC handling without lcms2 would need a custom patch that wires skcms (skcms_Parse / skcms_Transform, which ships with Skia) into PNGImageDecoder, JPEGImageDecoder and JPEGXLImageDecoder. Nothing like that exists in the tree.

Recommended doc change: add USE_LCMS=OFF to the flag table, and replace the reason with "accepting loss of embedded ICC handling (wrong colors for non-sRGB tagged images), or a custom skcms patch".

challenge.reasoning:
I agree with PARTIAL, but the reviewer's reason for the macOS problem needs correcting.

Windows: CONFIRMED. The upstream Win port uses Skia with ANGLE's EGL/GLES, and ANGLE builds static by default.

Linux: CONFIRMED. GTK and WPE only turn ANGLE on when WebGL is on (USE_ANGLE = ENABLE_WEBGL). Skia's GL goes through libepoxy, or through system EGL when libepoxy is off.

macOS: the reviewer says macOS needs ANGLE "unless you add a Metal backend". The doc already plans Metal for macOS (ZeroG.md:201, macOS | Metal), so the reviewer missed that. Still, the doc's statement "macOS only for WebGL" does not hold for the pinned tree without patches:
(a) WebKit's Skia CMake hard-codes Ganesh-GL only (SK_GL, SK_ASSUME_GL_ES=1) and lists no Metal sources. Skia's own Metal sources (src/gpu/ganesh/mtl/*.mm) are in the checkout but are never compiled.
(b) WebCore/CMakeLists.txt always links EGL/GLES. Without ANGLE and libepoxy it falls back to OpenGL::GLES plus EGL_LIBRARIES, and macOS has neither.
(c) PlatformDisplaySkia.cpp, which is in SourcesSkia.txt, includes <EGL/egl.h> and the EGL-backed GLContext whenever Skia is used.

So a Metal-only macOS build without ANGLE needs real port work: add the Metal sources and SK_METAL to the Skia CMake, keep EGL/GLES out of WebCore, and write a non-EGL PlatformDisplay. Otherwise ANGLE (whose Metal backend is in-tree as ANGLE/Metal.cmake) is effectively needed on macOS too. The same applies to the doc's Linux Vulkan option, since SK_VULKAN is not wired up either.

Smaller corrections to the reviewer's DLL list: d3dcompiler_47.dll ships with Windows 8.1 and later, so it is a system DLL loaded at runtime with LoadLibrary, not something you redistribute. d3d9, dxgi, dxguid and synchronization are system import libraries. The doc's Windows runtime list (kernel32, user32, d3d11, dxgi, crypt32, ws2_32) is incomplete, but nothing on it is a non-system DLL.

Also, without libepoxy, Skia and WebCore link EGL/GLES directly at link time (Skia CMakeLists.txt:865 links EGL_LIBRARIES). That clashes with the doc's "dlopen" claim for Linux drivers (doc line 199).

challenge.reasoning:
The PARTIAL verdict holds, and I couldn't refute it. The doc (ZeroG.md:428) says that in upstream ports the backend for `<video>`, `<audio>` and Web Audio "is GStreamer or AVFoundation". For `<video>`/`<audio>` that is wrong. The Windows port turns on a Media Foundation engine whenever ENABLE_VIDEO is on (it is on by default). That engine is registered in MediaPlayer.cpp, and the same port's default renderer is Skia, which the engine has a paint path for. For Web Audio the doc is actually right: the only AudioDestination::create implementations are Cocoa and GStreamer, and Windows turns ENABLE_WEB_AUDIO off. So the claim is half right.

The reviewer's follow-on conclusion goes too far, though. Adding an FFmpeg engine is not just a small edit to buildMediaEnginesVector. You also need: (1) a new value in two enums, MediaEngineIdentifier (MediaPlayerEnums.h) and MediaPlayerType (MediaPlayer.h); (2) a full MediaPlayerPrivateInterface plus a factory; (3) a separate AudioDestination::create backend if Web Audio is wanted, because there is no Windows or FFmpeg one upstream; (4) MSE is off on Windows (ENABLE_MEDIA_SOURCE OFF), so the Media Foundation engine only handles plain file/URL playback. Gotchas for reusing the Media Foundation engine in ZeroG: it is built on Direct3D 9 / DXVA2, not D3D11. Its Skia path copies a D3D9 memory surface into Skia in software. It needs an HWND from HostWindow::platformPageClient(), so ZeroG's ChromeClient must return a real HWND. It links mf/mfplat/mfuuid/d3d9 as delay-loaded DLLs. MediaPlayer.cpp also has a remote-engine registration hook (RemoteMediaPlayerSupport::registerRemoteEngineIfAvailable) meant for the multi-process setup; ZeroG has one process and can ignore it.

claims.claim: Profile 'minimal' = no media, no WebGL, reduced ICU data; 'dev' = Web Inspector
claims.evidence: The flags exist as described above. Several defaults are ON and must be set OFF explicitly: VIDEO, WEB_AUDIO, WEBGL, WEBASSEMBLY, XSLT, REMOTE_INSPECTOR, USE_AVIF, USE_JPEGXL, USE_LCMS. Other defaults are ON and need client or platform code rather than libraries: ENABLE_NOTIFICATIONS, GEOLOCATION, CONTEXT_MENUS, FULLSCREEN_API, MATHML, SMOOTH_SCROLLING, USER_MESSAGE_HANDLERS (WebKitFeatures.cmake:242-325). claims.implication: Write the defaults in your own OptionsZeroG.cmake with WEBKIT_OPTION_DEFAULT_PORT_VALUE, not as -D flags.

challenge.reasoning:
I tried to show the reviewer wrong and could not. Their verdict and flag inventory are correct, but they missed a few things that matter.

What the doc says (ZeroG.md:435-437): minimal = no media, no WebGL, reduced ICU data; standard = adds WebGL and, when it exists, the media backend; dev = full symbols, asserts on, Web Inspector enabled.

1) "No media / no WebGL" is CONFIRMED. These are ordinary WEBKIT_OPTIONs, but they default to ON, so the port has to turn them off. The media sub-features are already OFF and depend on VIDEO, so turning VIDEO off turns them off automatically. Other ports already do this through WEBKIT_OPTION_DEFAULT_PORT_VALUE: PlayStation sets WEB_AUDIO and WEBGL OFF, and Win sets WEBGL OFF. That supports the reviewer's advice to set defaults in an OptionsZeroG.cmake. The reviewer's list of ON defaults is accurate. They left out USE_WOFF2, which is also ON and pulls in libwoff2/brotli, and VIDEO_USES_ELEMENT_FULLSCREEN, which is ON but drops out once VIDEO is OFF. WEBASSEMBLY is only ON when C_LOOP is off, which is the case on x86_64 and arm64.

2) "Reduced ICU data" is UNVERIFIABLE from the checkout and is not a WebKit feature. No WebKit CMake option, script or variable trims ICU data. OptionsWin.cmake just requires find_package(ICU 70.1 REQUIRED COMPONENTS data i18n uc), and the tree has nothing for icudt, ICU_DATA filters or U_STATIC_IMPLEMENTATION apart from an Apple icucore lookup in FindICU.cmake. ZeroG would have to build ICU itself with an ICU data filter and check that WebCore still works with the trimmed data: line breaking, collation, IDNA, Intl in JSC.

3) "dev = asserts on, symbols" is CONFIRMED as possible. OptionsCommon.cmake:346-355 has an ENABLE_ASSERTS cache variable (AUTO/ON/OFF) that adds -DASSERT_ENABLED. DEVELOPER_MODE is a separate switch that other ports pass through (OptionsWin.cmake:132, OptionsGTK.cmake:76), and it changes compiler flags (WebKitCompilerFlags.cmake:166-180).

4) "dev = Web Inspector enabled" is PARTIAL. It is more than flipping a flag:
(a) Two separate switches are involved. ENABLE_REMOTE_INSPECTOR (WebKitFeatures.cmake:309, ON by default) controls the backend transport. ENABLE_WEBINSPECTORUI is a plain variable, not a WEBKIT_OPTION. It defaults to ON in WebKitCommon.cmake:68-69 and is set OFF by PlayStation and JSCOnly. It adds the WebInspectorUI subdirectory (Source/CMakeLists.txt:72-80) and makes WebCore depend on it (WebCore/CMakeLists.txt:3163-3165). So a minimal profile has to set ENABLE_WEBINSPECTORUI OFF explicitly, or every build compiles the frontend.
(b) The WebInspectorUI build runs Perl and Python (copy-user-interface-resources.pl, WebInspectorUI/CMakeLists.txt:82), and each port has its own resource packaging file (PlatformWin/GTK/WPE/Cocoa.cmake). ZeroG would need its own, for example to serve the files over app:// or embed them.
(c) This is the main thing the doc misses. The object that exposes a page to the inspector is not in WebCore. It exists as WebKit/UIProcess/Inspector/WebPageDebuggable.h:39 (WebKit2) and WebKitLegacy/WebCoreSupport/LegacyWebPageDebuggable.h:38, and ZeroG builds neither. ZeroG must write its own Inspector::RemoteInspectionTarget for its page, plus either an in-process frontend client based on WebCore/inspector/InspectorFrontendClientLocal.h:52 or the socket remote-inspector server (JavaScriptCore/inspector/remote/Socket.cmake, which has win and posix socket files). On Windows the JSC hook is PlatformWin.cmake:10.
(d) ENABLE_REMOTE_INSPECTOR is a compile-time define that affects JSC, so dev and non-dev builds are separate builds of the whole engine. That is fine for build profiles.

Net: the media/WebGL part is confirmed with the extra work above, the ICU part is external and unverifiable, and the inspector part needs port code the doc does not mention. PARTIAL stands.

The vendored Skia CMake hard-requires Fontconfig and FreeType on every non-Windows target (ThirdParty/skia/CMakeLists.txt:4-6, 845-852). WebCore Skia font code calls SkFontMgr_New_FontConfig and FcFontSort directly outside Windows and Android (FontCacheSkia.cpp:70; SkiaSystemFallbackFontCache.cpp:29-110). Removing Fontconfig means new code, not a dependency swap.

The vendored Skia CMake builds only Ganesh GL/GLES (SK_GL, SK_GANESH, SK_ASSUME_GL_ES=1 at :1070-1086). It has no Metal, Vulkan, D3D or Graphite, although those sources are in the tree. It does build the PDF backend unconditionally (src/pdf from :611).

WebCore's CMake always links some GL stack: ANGLE EGL/GLES, or libepoxy, or OpenGL::GLES + EGL_LIBRARIES (WebCore/CMakeLists.txt:2299-2316). On Linux that means a link-time dependency on libEGL and libGLESv2, not dlopen. On macOS there is no system EGL, so ANGLE (which has Metal.cmake) is effectively mandatory.

HarfBuzz must be built with its ICU bridge (libharfbuzz-icu). WebCore links HarfBuzz::ICU (platform/Skia.cmake) and calls hb_icu_script_to_script (ComplexTextControllerSkia.cpp:265; LocaleICU.cpp:82).

libwebp is not optional. WEBPImageDecoder is compiled unconditionally and WebP::demux is always linked (platform/ImageDecoders.cmake). Skia encoders need WebP::mux, and static builds need libsharpyuv (OptionsWin.cmake:168, PlatformWin.cmake:247-248).

WebCore uses zlib directly, beyond HTTP and PNG: CompressionStream (Modules/compression/ZStream.h), WebSocket permessage-deflate (WebSocketDeflater.cpp), and WOFF1 (WOFFFileFormat.cpp). ANGLE links zlib as well.

FreeType built with brotli (FT_CONFIG_OPTION_USE_BROTLI) sets HAVE_WOFF_SUPPORT and makes libwoff2 unnecessary wherever Skia rasterizes through FreeType (WOFF2Checks.cmake; OptionsGTK.cmake:413-421; FontCustomPlatformDataSkia.cpp:139). Windows Skia uses DirectWrite, so libwoff2 is still needed there, linked together with Brotli::dec and WOFF2::common (PlatformWin.cmake:236-244).

On Windows, the upstream Skia build uses DirectWrite (skia/CMakeLists.txt:815-827, SK_TYPEFACE_FACTORY_DIRECTWRITE), not FreeType. Using FreeType on Windows for embedded fonts means changing Skia's CMake and WebCore's FontCacheSkiaWin.cpp.

No upstream CMake port builds WebCore with ENABLE_VIDEO=OFF. PlayStation keeps VIDEO ON with no media engine, Windows uses Media Foundation. VIDEO=OFF is untested and likely has bit-rot, while 'VIDEO ON with no engine' is a tested configuration.

Web Audio needs platform code that exists only for Cocoa and GStreamer: AudioDestination, FFTFrame (there is an FFTFrameStub) and AudioFileReader. A media player backend alone is not enough for the 'standard' profile.
Media engines are registered in hard-coded code (MediaPlayer.cpp:326-367), so a custom FFmpeg engine means patching buildMediaEnginesVector.

The curl network glue (NetworkDataTaskCurl, NetworkSessionCurl, NetworkStorageSessionCurl) lives in Source/WebKit/NetworkProcess/curl, not WebCore. WebCore has no ResourceHandleCurl.cpp, so the single-process port must provide its own loader on top of WebCore's CurlRequest.

curl must use an OpenSSL-API TLS backend: WebCore installs a CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION and works with SSL_CTX* (CurlSSLVerifier.cpp:41-49). It also RELEASE_ASSERTs CURL_VERSION_LARGEFILE (CurlContext.cpp:129) and automatically uses HTTP/3 if curl supports it (CurlContext.cpp:133-134).

MIME type lookup needs a platform implementation. GLib ports use the vendored ThirdParty/xdgmime (USE_XDGMIME), Win uses MIMETypeRegistryWin.cpp, PlayStation uses MIMETypeRegistryPlayStation.cpp (a static table, the likely model for ZeroG).

JSC still reserves large virtual ranges even with system malloc: a 1 GB executable pool on x86_64 and 128 or 512 MB on arm64 (jit/ExecutableAllocator.cpp:94-104), plus an aligned structure heap (heap/StructureAlignedMemoryAllocator.cpp:99-112, tunable through Options::structureHeapSizeInKB).

Upstream Find modules (FindWebP, FindWOFF2, FindBrotli, FindLibPSL) create UNKNOWN IMPORTED targets with no static transitive dependencies. In a fully static build you must add brotlicommon, sharpyuv, zlib (for png and freetype) and similar libs by hand, as PlatformWin.cmake already does.

Minimum versions enforced by the upstream Options files: ICU 70.1, CURL 7.87.0, HarfBuzz 1.4.2 (Win) / 2.7.4 (WPE), JPEG 1.5.2, LibXml2 2.9.7 (Win) / 2.9.13 (GLib ports), PNG 1.6.34, SQLite3 3.23.1, ZLIB 1.2.11, LibPSL 0.20.2, Freetype 2.9.0, WOFF2 1.0.2, Fontconfig 2.13.0.

Required build-time tools: Perl 5.10 with English, FindBin and JSON::PP; Python; Ruby; gperf 3.0.1 (only with WebCore) (WebKitCommon.cmake:277-290, 370). unifdef is vendored (Source/CMakeLists.txt:19-22). Source/WebGPU is always added, for its headers only (Source/CMakeLists.txt:27-28).

External, not verifiable in this checkout: libpsl's official build is meson/autotools and generating its builtin list needs Python; ICU has no CMake build and data filtering needs ICU's Python buildtool; libjpeg-turbo SIMD needs NASM. These conflict with criterion 2 ('si compila statica con CMake o zig') and need custom build scripts.

claims.claim: The port is added as a new value of PORT in WebKit's CMake
claims.evidence: Source/cmake/WebKitCommon.cmake:76-95 has a hardcoded `set(ALL_PORTS Cocoa GTK IOS JSCOnly Mac PlayStation WPE Win)`, and any other value hits `message(FATAL_ERROR "Please choose which WebKit port to build...")`. Top-level CMakeLists.txt:9-25 sets CMAKE_MODULE_PATH=Source/cmake, then calls project() and include(WebKitCommon). On a Darwin host, Source/cmake/WebKitXcodeSDK.cmake:111-121 runs before project() and fails with FATAL_ERROR for any PORT other than Mac/Cocoa/JSCOnly/empty unless CMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT is passed.
claims.implication: Adding PORT=ZeroG means patching WebKitCommon.cmake (ALL_PORTS). That is an upstream-file patch and belongs in patches/. On macOS, either pass -DCMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT or also patch WebKitXcodeSDK.cmake.

challenge.reasoning:
I tried to prove the other reviewer wrong and couldn't. Adding a new PORT value is how WebKit ports are wired up: Options${PORT}.cmake is included by name and Platform${PORT}.cmake files are picked up in each directory. So the design is the right approach. It is not purely additive, though, and the doc implies it is. Three upstream-tree changes are unavoidable:
(1) WebKitCommon.cmake builds ALL_PORTS as a local variable inside the file and then calls list(FIND). Any other value hits FATAL_ERROR. The list is set with a plain set(), not a cache variable, so passing -DALL_PORTS cannot override it. The only bypass is pre-setting HAS_RUN_WEBKIT_COMMON, which skips the whole file and is useless.
(2) The include(Options${PORT}) lookup goes through CMAKE_MODULE_PATH. The top-level CMakeLists.txt overwrites that path with set(), so it is not appended to and cannot be extended from the command line. OptionsZeroG.cmake therefore has to sit physically in Source/cmake, unless a custom top-level CMakeLists is used. That route is fragile because WebKitCommon uses CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR for Tools, WebKitBuild and compile_commands.
(3) WEBKIT_INCLUDE_CONFIG_FILES_IF_EXISTS looks only in ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/Platform${PORT}.cmake. Every PlatformZeroG.cmake must be dropped into the upstream directories themselves. A missing file only produces a STATUS message, not an error, so it silently builds the wrong thing.
This clashes with the doc's rule (L103) that new port code lives in its own directories and only patches/ touches upstream. The doc also lists WTF/JSC/WebCore only, but the same include hook exists in bmalloc, PAL, the Source/ root and others. bmalloc and WebGPU are always added. The macOS SDK gate is real: an unknown PORT on a Darwin host fails before project() unless CMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT is set. There is also a nuance in favour of the doc: Mac and IOS are now aliases folded into Cocoa (lines 98-100), so the list is literally editable. Still, the reviewer's reading is accurate, and PARTIAL stands.
challenge.evidence:

Lines 85-94: PORT cache var defaults to NOPORT, list(FIND ALL_PORTS ${PORT} RET), and if RET == -1 it calls message(FATAL_ERROR "Please choose which WebKit port to build..."), except on APPLE with NOPORT, which becomes Cocoa. Lines 98-100: Mac and IOS are folded into Cocoa. Line 102: WEBKIT_PORT_DIR = tolower(PORT). Lines 6-7: the whole file is guarded by HAS_RUN_WEBKIT_COMMON. Line 12: PORT is an identity var stamped in .webkit-config-stamp and must not change after the first configure (lines 28-32).
- WebKitCommon.cmake:356-357: include(OptionsCommon) then include(Options${PORT}), resolved through CMAKE_MODULE_PATH. Existing files in Source/cmake: OptionsCocoa, OptionsCommon, OptionsGTK, OptionsJSCOnly, OptionsMSVC, OptionsPlayStation, OptionsWPE, OptionsWin.

challenge.reasoning:
I tried to refute the reviewer and couldn't. Their verdict stands, and they missed one blocker that matters more than anything they found.

How the mechanism works: there is one global Options${PORT}.cmake, loaded from Source/cmake through CMAKE_MODULE_PATH. Each component then gets its own optional Platform${PORT}.cmake, which is picked up from CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR only if the file exists. So the doc's wording "Options<Port>.cmake and Platform<Port>.cmake for WTF, JavaScriptCore and WebCore" is wrong in two ways:
(a) Options is not per component. It is a single Source/cmake/OptionsZeroG.cmake.
(b) The set of Platform files needed is wider than WTF, JSC and WebCore. PAL is effectively required: it provides the CryptoDigest backend. The PlayStation model also ships bmalloc, JSC shell, testmem, ANGLE, gtest, WebDriver, WebKit, Tools and other Platform files.

The reviewer's small errors: their line numbers for WebKitCommon are off by about 10 (it is 356-357, not 346-347). They also said WTF's common list has no RunLoop/MainThread/FileSystem/Threading sources. In fact it has the shared halves (RunLoop.cpp, MainThread.cpp, FileSystem.cpp, Threading.cpp). What it lacks are the platform backends (generic/RunLoopGeneric.cpp, posix/ThreadingPOSIX.cpp, posix/FileSystemPOSIX.cpp, OSAllocator*.cpp). Their conclusion still holds: WTF/wtf/PlatformZeroG.cmake is mandatory.

What the reviewer and the doc both missed:
1. PORT is checked against a hard-coded ALL_PORTS list in WebKitCommon.cmake. Running with PORT=ZeroG stops with FATAL_ERROR, so WebKitCommon.cmake itself must be patched. Adding new files is not enough.
2. The top-level CMakeLists.txt:10 uses set(), not list(APPEND), for CMAKE_MODULE_PATH. That overwrites anything passed from outside, so an out-of-tree OptionsZeroG.cmake can't be found without a patch or an overlay. Together with the CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR lookup for Platform files, "keep ZeroG code in its own directories" means keeping an overlay/copy step or a patch set against the upstream tree.
3. WEBKIT_PORT_DIR is set to the lowercased port name ('zerog'), which some code uses to build paths.
4. Source/CMakeLists.txt always adds bmalloc, WTF, JavaScriptCore and WebGPU (its comment says WebCore uses the WebGPU C++ API header even with WebGPU disabled). WebCore, WebKitLegacy, WebKit and WebDriver are gated by ENABLE_WEBCORE, ENABLE_WEBKIT_LEGACY, ENABLE_WEBKIT and ENABLE_WEBDRIVER, which OptionsZeroG must set (ENABLE_WEBKIT=OFF for no WebKit2). USE_SKIA turns on the bundled ThirdParty/skia.

challenge.reasoning:
I checked every line the reviewer cited and could not refute any of them. The structural half of the claim is true. PlayStation is an upstream CMake PORT. It has Source/cmake/OptionsPlayStation.cmake and Platform<Port>.cmake files for WTF, JavaScriptCore, WebCore and PAL (and also for bmalloc, WebKit, WebDriver, ANGLE and gtest). Its WTF uses generic/RunLoopGeneric.cpp, its WebCore network layer is curl+OpenSSL, and it has the ENABLE_STATIC_JSC option. So "Options<Port>.cmake + Platform<Port>.cmake modelled on PlayStation" is an accurate picture of the layout.

PlayStation is not a clean template to copy, though, so PARTIAL stands:
(1) OptionsPlayStation.cmake:7-8 includes PlayStationModule and Sign. Neither exists in the tree; the only match is the include line itself. Copying the file also brings in -sce-stdlib=v2 (:25), WEBKIT_LIBRARIES_DIR / WebKitRequirements (:31-37, :91-94), a pkg-config kill-switch (:44-49), mmap wrapping (:390-401) and signing.
(2) WTF/wtf/PlatformPlayStation.cmake:39 and WebCore/PlatformPlayStation.cmake:175 call PLAYSTATION_COPY_MODULES, a macro defined only in OptionsPlayStation.cmake:449. The Platform files will not configure without it.
(3) WebCore links WPE::libwpe unconditionally (:80-82). It also compiles the libwpe sources EditorLibWPE, PasteboardLibWPE, PlatformKeyboardEventLibWPE and GLContextLibWPE, and always includes TextureMapper.cmake. OptionsPlayStation forces USE_LIBWPE ON, USE_TEXTURE_MAPPER ON, and USE_COORDINATED_GRAPHICS ON when there is no GPU process (:273, :316, :329).
(4) USE_SKIA defaults to OFF in WebKitFeatures.cmake:363, and OptionsPlayStation never turns it on, so PlayStation builds Cairo by default (:276-281). Only the GTK, WPE and Win Options files default USE_SKIA ON. PlatformPlayStation does have a USE_SKIA branch that includes Skia.cmake (WebCore/PlatformPlayStation.cmake:6-11), so Skia is wired in but off by default.
(5) PlayStation is never configured as fully static. WebKit_LIBRARY_TYPE is SHARED (:374), and JSC is only OBJECT when ENABLE_STATIC_JSC is on (:362-366).
(6) The JIT is off by default (:176-178).

The doc also misses a hard prerequisite. Adding a new PORT value means patching upstream Source/cmake/WebKitCommon.cmake. Its hard-coded ALL_PORTS list (Cocoa, GTK, IOS, JSCOnly, Mac, PlayStation, WPE, Win) calls FATAL_ERROR on any other port name, so this is one more downstream patch to carry. Two more gaps: the WTF platform file pulls in playstation/FileSystemPlayStation, LanguagePlayStation, OSAllocatorPlayStation and UniStdExtrasPlayStation, which ZeroG has to replace with posix/win/cocoa versions for each OS. And for "Skia on by default plus Windows", the Win port is the better reference, since OptionsWin.cmake:91 sets USE_SKIA ON.

challenge.reasoning:
The PARTIAL verdict holds. I could not show the reviewer wrong on any point. A new PORT with Options/Platform<Port>.cmake files is possible: PORT is chosen from the ALL_PORTS list, and the build then runs include(Options${PORT}). But the claim that "the same configuration works for Linux, Windows and macOS, and OS differences live only in the platform layer" is false as written. Which PLATFORM() macro you get is decided in WTF/bmalloc headers based on the host OS, not by the PORT variable.

1) Copying the PlayStation model does not work on Windows or macOS. PlayStation only adds -DWTF_PLATFORM_PLAYSTATION=1 and -DBPLATFORM_PLAYSTATION=1 on the command line and never touches PlatformLegacy.h. That is enough there only because the PlayStation OS is neither OS(MACOS) nor OS(WINDOWS), so the #elif chain in PlatformLegacy.h defines nothing else. A ZeroG build that just adds -DWTF_PLATFORM_ZEROG=1 would still get WTF_PLATFORM_WIN on Windows, and WTF_PLATFORM_MAC plus COCOA on macOS. COCOA in turn sets USE_CF, USE_FOUNDATION and includes PlatformEnableCocoa.h; PLATFORM(WIN) includes PlatformEnableWin.h. So a header patch, or reusing BUILDING_JSCONLY__, really is required, as the reviewer said.

2) The reviewer's fix is incomplete for bmalloc on macOS. In BPlatform.h, BPLATFORM_MAC (and BOS_MAC) are set without any condition inside the BOS(DARWIN)/TARGET_OS_MAC block at lines 97-99. That block is outside the BUILDING_* chain at lines 121-129, so adding a ZEROG branch to that chain stops only BPLATFORM_WIN, not BPLATFORM_MAC/COCOA. Even JSCOnly gets BPLATFORM(MAC) on macOS today. You either accept that or patch the Darwin block too (or turn bmalloc off, as the allocator section discusses).

3) More facts the doc misses: ZeroG must be added to ALL_PORTS in WebKitCommon.cmake, or configure stops with a FATAL_ERROR. OptionsJSCOnly.cmake has to branch on MSVC, WIN32 and APPLE, and WTF/wtf/PlatformJSCOnly.cmake has separate source lists for WIN32, APPLE, Linux, FreeBSD and other systems, so the cmake files are per-OS too, not only the C++ platform layer. 170 WebCore files test PLATFORM(WIN), which matches the reviewer's count.

challenge.reasoning:
PARTIAL still holds, but part of the reviewer's evidence is wrong. They said the option is defined in only two places and has "no other uses in the tree". The definitions part is correct: only OptionsPlayStation.cmake:173 and OptionsJSCOnly.cmake:19 define it. The "no other uses" part is false. WEBKIT_OPTION_DEFINE passes the option to C++ as a macro (ENABLE_STATIC_JSC / ENABLE(STATIC_JSC)), and 7 PlayStation-only C++ files use it to skip dlopen-ing libJavaScriptCore when JSC is linked in.

Those guards back up the doc's history claim, though only indirectly. The option drives real logic only in PlayStation code. Its PlayStation description, "Control whether to build a non-shared JSC", is word-for-word the doc's "non-shared" phrasing. JSCOnly defines it with a different description and default OFF, which looks like it was added later.

The commit history and the 2021 mailing-list link cannot be checked: the checkout is shallow and lists.webkit.org returned HTTP 403.

Why the claim is only partly right: "the CMake build has an option" makes it sound global. It is not in WebKitFeatures.cmake or WebKitCommon.cmake; each port defines it in its own Options file. A new PORT=ZeroG would not have it unless OptionsZeroG.cmake defines it.

The reviewer's practical advice is correct. WebKitCommon.cmake:240-244 already defaults bmalloc, WTF, JavaScriptCore, PAL and WebCore to STATIC, so ZeroG needs no such option. For a JSCOnly bring-up, -DENABLE_STATIC_JSC=ON keeps STATIC for all; OFF makes JSC SHARED and WTF/bmalloc OBJECT (OptionsJSCOnly.cmake:52-56).

Gotchas the doc misses:
(a) On PlayStation, "non-shared" means OBJECT libraries, not .a archives. The comment at OptionsPlayStation.cmake:355-358 says OBJECT emulates --whole-archive so all exports are exposed. ZeroG will hit the same issue: unreferenced JSC/WebCore symbols or static initializers can be dropped from a static archive. That matters if the C API and symbol exports must survive the final zig link (use OBJECT libraries or --whole-archive / /WHOLEARCHIVE).
(b) PlayStation also sets PAL/WebCore to OBJECT because libWebCore.a is "too much for ranlib" (OptionsPlayStation.cmake:368-372). This is a real size/tooling risk for a fully static WebCore archive, especially on Windows lib.exe / llvm-lib.
(c) If OptionsZeroG defines ENABLE_STATIC_JSC, C++ will see ENABLE(STATIC_JSC); otherwise ENABLE(STATIC_JSC) evaluates to 0. That only matters if ZeroG reuses PlayStation-style entry-point code.

claims.evidence: WebKitCommon.cmake:232-243 makes bmalloc/WTF/JSC/PAL/WebCore/WebCoreTestSupport STATIC by default and only WebKit/WebKitLegacy SHARED. No current port actually ships WebCore STATIC: GTK/WPE use OBJECT (OptionsGTK:216-218, OptionsWPE:187-190), PlayStation uses OBJECT ('The size of a libWebCore.a is too much for ranlib', OptionsPlayStation.cmake:368-373), and Win uses SHARED (OptionsWin.cmake:184-189). WebKitMacros.cmake:149-151 keeps an MSVC+STATIC WebCore special case ('helps keep WebCore.lib's size below the 4GB maximum in debug builds'). OptionsMSVC.cmake:1 says 'WebKit dropped MSVC support. This file is only for clang-cl.' It uses clang-only flags (/clang:-masm=att :76, /Zc:dllexportInlines- :117) and does find_library(clang_rt.builtins-x86_64 ... REQUIRED) under <clang-cl>/../lib/clang/<major>/lib/windows (:128-141). GCC>=13.1 is enforced (WebKitCommon.cmake:132-136). There is a Clang<19 workaround (WebKitCompilerFlags.cmake:243-251), which implies Clang 18 is the floor.
claims.implication: Static archives work in principle but are untested upstream for WebCore. Expect a .lib >4GB in Debug on Windows and ranlib/ar trouble on Linux. Plan on OBJECT libraries plus your own archiving or final link step. clang-cl is required in practice: cl.exe fails at the clang_rt.builtins lookup and on clang-only flags.

challenge.reasoning:
I tried to overturn the reviewer and could not. The PARTIAL verdict holds; I am only correcting a few details. WebKit's CMake does let a custom PORT build WTF, JSC and WebCore as STATIC; that is the fallback default. But no upstream port actually ships WebCore as STATIC. GTK, WPE and PlayStation build WebCore as OBJECT, Win as SHARED and Cocoa as SHARED. PlayStation says outright that libWebCore.a is too big for ranlib. Upstream also tells clang-cl apart from cl.exe and drops cl.exe ("WebKit dropped MSVC support").

Corrections and additions to the reviewer:
(1) The line numbers are slightly off. The defaults block is WebKitCommon.cmake:241-248 (the comment starts at 237), and the 4GB comment is WebKitMacros.cmake:150-153.
(2) The reviewer missed something that supports the doc. OptionsJSCOnly.cmake:19 defines a PUBLIC option ENABLE_STATIC_JSC (default OFF). Lines 52-55 only switch to SHARED JSC and OBJECT bmalloc/WTF when that option is OFF. So static bmalloc, WTF and JSC is a configuration upstream supports and keeps building. The "untested static" risk applies only to WebCore and PAL.
(3) Gotcha for the new port: OptionsMSVC.cmake is not pulled in globally. Only OptionsWin.cmake:1-3 and OptionsJSCOnly.cmake:3-4 include it, under if (MSVC). A new OptionsZeroG.cmake must include(OptionsMSVC) itself, or the clang-cl setup is lost: /clang:-masm=att, /GR-, no exceptions, /bigobj, /Zc:dllexportInlines-, the clang_rt.builtins link and the 8MB stack.
(4) CMake sets MSVC to true for clang-cl too. So the special case at WebKitMacros.cmake:151, which raises the bundle size to keep WebCore.lib under 4GB, fires for a clang-cl STATIC WebCore. That confirms a static WebCore on Windows is near the COFF archive size limit in Debug.
(5) "Clang 18 floor" is an inference, not an enforced check. The comment at WebKitCompilerFlags.cmake:243 only says Clang 18 is still supported for GTK and WPE. No version check makes the build fail for older Clang. Only GCC has a hard check: GCC 13.1 or newer, FATAL_ERROR, at WebKitCommon.cmake:134-136.
(6) The cross-compile path in OptionsMSVC looks for llvm-lib, llvm-rc and llvm-ranlib (versions -20 or unversioned) when the host is Linux (OptionsMSVC.cmake:41-50). This is useful if CI cross-builds Windows from Linux.

Net: the claim holds for WTF and JSC. For WebCore it is technically possible but not exercised upstream, and there are documented archive-size problems. That makes it PARTIAL.

claims.claim: Static C++ runtime, independent of the version installed on the system
claims.doc_section: Build system e linking statico / Struttura
claims.evidence: No WebKit CMake file uses -static-libstdc++, -static-libgcc or -stdlib=libc++ (grep over Source/cmake). OptionsMSVC.cmake:57-58 hard-sets `set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY MultiThreadedDLL)`, a normal variable that shadows any -D cache value.
claims.implication: Linux: the final link must pass -static-libstdc++ (or a static libc++) itself. Windows: OptionsZeroG must re-set CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY to MultiThreaded after include(OptionsMSVC), and every dependency must be built /MT.

challenge.reasoning:
The claim (ZeroG.md:424, "Runtime C++ statico") is a goal of the design. It is achievable, but upstream WebKit does nothing to support it, so the ZeroG port has to build it. I could not find anything the reviewer missed that would make it CONFIRMED.

(1) Linux/generic: nothing in WebKit's own build files (Source/cmake) uses -static-libstdc++, -static-libgcc or -stdlib=libc++. OptionsCommon.cmake:278-313 only checks which standard library is in use (libc++ >= 19 or libstdc++) to pick hardening macros. It never selects or statically links one. The only static-runtime flags in the tree are inside bundled third-party projects (ANGLE's VK-GL-CTS CFlags.cmake:106-107, MinGW only; and boringssl's benchmark CMakeLists.txt:295), so they don't affect WebCore/JSC.

(2) Windows: OptionsMSVC.cmake:58 unconditionally runs `set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY MultiThreadedDLL)`, citing Swift's release-only swiftrt.obj. This is a normal variable, so it hides any -D cache value. One thing the reviewer missed works in ZeroG's favour: OptionsMSVC is only included by the port option files themselves (OptionsWin.cmake:2, OptionsJSCOnly.cmake:4). So OptionsZeroG can skip that include, or override the variable after it. The top-level cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20) (CMakeLists.txt:9) means policy CMP0091 is NEW, so CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY="MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>" will work.

A second point the reviewer missed: the upstream vcpkg triplets also set VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE dynamic (WebKitLibraries/triplets/x64-windows-webkit.cmake:2, arm64-windows-webkit.cmake:2). The cross toolchain reads that value into CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY and puts /MD or /MT straight into the CMAKE_<LANG>_FLAGS_<CONFIG> cache entries (windows-cross.cmake:30, 86-89, 116-119). So every vcpkg dependency (ICU, curl, etc.) is built /MD by default, and ZeroG needs its own triplet with static CRT. Mixing /MT and /MD objects causes LNK2038 mismatch errors. Swift interop would have to stay disabled, or ZeroG accepts /MD.

(3) A nuance the doc misses: on macOS, Apple ships no static libc++. libc++.dylib is part of the OS. A "static C++ runtime" there means building and bundling your own libc++/libc++abi, or (more realistically) accepting the system dylib, which has a stable ABI. The doc's Linux plan of building with zig (ZeroG.md:518) does help: zig c++ bundles libc++/libc++abi and links them statically by default. That is an external fact I could not check in the tree. It still needs a build to confirm that WebKit's libc++ >= 19 check and the hardening macros work with zig's libc++. The doc's own goal of keeping libc++ symbols internal (ZeroG.md:161) also needs hidden visibility or a symbol version script, and nothing in the tree provides one.

Net: the claim is feasible but none of it exists upstream, so PARTIAL stands.
challenge.evidence:
- Source/cmake/OptionsMSVC.cmake:57-58: `# Swift only ships a release-CRT swiftrt.obj ...` / `set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY MultiThreadedDLL)`, set unconditionally as a normal variable.
- Source/cmake/OptionsWin.cmake:2 and OptionsJSCOnly.cmake:4: these are the only places that include(OptionsMSVC), so a new OptionsZeroG.cmake decides whether to include it.
- CMakeLists.txt:9: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20), so CMP0091 is NEW and CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY is honoured.
- WebKitLibraries/triplets/x64-windows-webkit.cmake:2 and arm64-windows-webkit.cmake:2: `set(VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE dynamic)`.
- WebKitLibraries/toolchains/windows-cross.cmake:30: CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY is set as a cache value from VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE. Lines 86-89 pick /MD or /MT, and lines 116-119 put that flag directly into CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG/RELEASE.
- Source/cmake/OptionsCommon.cmake:278-313: only detects libc++ (requires >= 19) or libstdc++ for the hardening macros. There is no -stdlib or static flag anywhere in Source/cmake.
- The only static-runtime flags in the tree are in third-party code: Source/ThirdParty/ANGLE/third_party/VK-GL-CTS/src/framework/delibs/cmake/CFlags.cmake:106-107 (MinGW -static-libstdc++) and Source/ThirdParty/libwebrtc/Source/third_party/boringssl/src/third_party/benchmark/CMakeLists.txt:295 (-stdlib=libc++).
- Bundled third-party projects pick their own CRT: Source/ThirdParty/capstone/Source/CMakeLists.txt:132 forces /MT. abseil (CMakeLists.txt:65-67) and opus (CMakeLists.txt:276-278) choose /MT or /MD based on an option, so they must be built consistently.
- ZeroG.md:424 states the goal, ZeroG.md:519 says Windows uses a static CRT (`/MT`), ZeroG.md:518 says Linux is built with zig against an old glibc, and ZeroG.md:161 says the engine's libc++ symbols must stay internal. The doc says nothing about macOS.

claims.claim: zig build runs CMake as an external step and collects the archives
claims.doc_section: Build system e linking statico / Struttura
claims.evidence: OptionsCommon.cmake:167-182: when ar and ld support it, USE_THIN_ARCHIVES defaults ON (crT), so the .a files only reference .o files in the build tree. WebKitMacros.cmake:409-437: with COMPILER_IS_CLANG AND NOT MSVC AND NOT CMAKE_DISABLE_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS, WEBKIT_DEFINE_SUBTARGET_WITH_PREFIX moves sources into separate OBJECT libraries. For non-SHARED parents these are attached only as `target_link_libraries(${_target} INTERFACE ${_subobjects})`, so they are not inside the archive. Affected: JavaScriptCoreJIT (jit dfg ftl bytecode bytecompiler llint lol tools, JSC CMakeLists.txt:1882-1885) and WebCoreJSBindings/Style/DOMAndRendering/Inspector (WebCore CMakeLists.txt:3302-3324). LowLevelInterpreterLib is an OBJECT library (JSC CMakeLists.txt:503, 1874-1878). OptionsMSVC.cmake:81-83 uses add_link_options(/DEBUG /OPT:NOICF /OPT:REF), with the comment that ICF 'makes it unsafe to pointer-compare functions', and :143 sets /STACK:8388608 for executables.
claims.implication: Pass -DUSE_THIN_ARCHIVES=OFF. On Linux/macOS also pass -DCMAKE_DISABLE_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS=ON, or harvest $<TARGET_OBJECTS:JavaScriptCoreJIT> and the WebCore subtargets. Otherwise linking libJavaScriptCore.a/libWebCore.a outside CMake leaves undefined symbols. The final zig/lld-link step must replicate /OPT:NOICF (no identical-code folding), an 8MB main stack, clang_rt.builtins and the system libs.

challenge.reasoning:
The PARTIAL verdict holds. Running CMake as an external step and then linking its outputs from zig works in principle. But "collecting the archives" does not give you a complete link set. Two parts of WebKit's build in this checkout break it: thin archives, and PCH subtargets whose object files never go into the parent .a. I tried to break the reviewer's case and could not. Every cited file and line exists and says what they report, and the guards are read correctly. Three small corrections to their scope:

(1) LowLevelInterpreterLib is NOT a problem for a STATIC JavaScriptCore. It is passed as a direct PRIVATE target_link_libraries item of the JavaScriptCore target (JSC CMakeLists.txt:1877, applied by WebKitMacros.cmake:515). CMake (3.12 and later) puts the objects of a directly linked OBJECT library into the static archive. Only the subtarget objects, attached as INTERFACE generator-expression file lists (WebKitMacros.cmake:437), stay outside the archive. Listing LowLevelInterpreterLib among the "affected" items overstates the problem.

(2) Thin archives are mostly a Linux issue. They turn on only when the linker probe (`${CMAKE_C_COMPILER} -Wl,--version`) reports LLD, mold, gold or GNU ld, AND `ar -V` reports GNU ar or LLVM ar (OptionsCommon.cmake:51-58, 72-86, 129-140, 170-175). Apple ld64/cctools ar on macOS, and clang-cl/lld-link on Windows, should fall into the UNKNOWN branch, so thin archives default to OFF there. This is inferred from the code, not confirmed by running a configure. Even if the option were ON on Windows, the CMAKE_<LANG>_ARCHIVE_CREATE override at :178-181 is not the rule MSVC-style static libraries use.

(3) The PCH subtargets are disabled on Windows/clang-cl because the guard requires `NOT MSVC` (WebKitMacros.cmake:410). So on Windows the archives are complete with respect to subtargets, and on Linux/macOS with Clang they are not.

The MSVC link flags are confirmed as stated: no ICF, /OPT:REF, an 8 MB stack, and clang_rt.builtins added through link_libraries. A link done outside CMake has to reproduce all of them. The JavaScriptCoreJIT subtarget is not optional: its DIRS list includes llint, bytecode and jit, so on Linux/macOS a large share of JSC lives only in its object files.
challenge.evidence:
- third_party/webkit/Source/cmake/OptionsCommon.cmake:51-58: linker probe `${CMAKE_C_COMPILER} ... -Wl,--version`. :72-86: LD_SUPPORTS_THIN_ARCHIVES is TRUE only for LLD/mold/gold/BFD, otherwise UNKNOWN -> FALSE. :129-140: AR_SUPPORTS_THIN_ARCHIVES only when `ar -V` reports "GNU ar" or "LLVM". :170-175: `option(USE_THIN_ARCHIVES ... ${USE_THIN_ARCHIVES_DEFAULT})`. :177-181: CMAKE_{C,CXX}_ARCHIVE_CREATE = `<CMAKE_AR> crT ...`, APPEND = `rT`.

- third_party/webkit/Source/cmake/OptionsMSVC.cmake:81-83: `add_link_options(/DEBUG /OPT:NOICF /OPT:REF)`, with the comment that ICF "makes it unsafe to pointer-compare functions with identical definitions". :126: /INCREMENTAL:NO. :128-141: find_library(clang_rt.builtins-<arch>) REQUIRED, then link_libraries. :143: CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS += /STACK:8388608.
- What to do: on Linux pass -DUSE_THIN_ARCHIVES=OFF. On Linux/macOS with Clang, either pass -DCMAKE_DISABLE_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS=ON or export the object lists for the subtargets with file(GENERATE ... $<TARGET_OBJECTS:JavaScriptCoreJIT>/WebCore*), for example from a small CMake helper target. A cleaner option is to have CMake itself generate the final link line or a response file for zig. On Windows, reproduce /OPT:NOICF, /STACK:8388608 and clang_rt.builtins in the zig link step.

claims.evidence: WTF/wtf/PlatformJSCOnly.cmake:25-30 links DbgHelp, shlwapi, synchronization and winmm. JavaScriptCore/PlatformJSCOnly.cmake:41-45 links ws2_32. OptionsMSVC.cmake:138-141 adds link_libraries(clang_rt.builtins), which is static. OptionsJSCOnly.cmake:59 sets NTDDI_VERSION=0x0A000006 (Windows 10 1809). challenge.reasoning:
I tried to refute the reviewer and couldn't. The part of the claim saying only system DLLs are needed holds, because every library upstream links for WTF and JSC on Windows ships with the OS. The parenthetical list is incomplete, though. Each item the reviewer cited checks out:
- WTF links DbgHelp, shlwapi, synchronization and winmm.
- JSC links ws2_32.
- clang_rt.builtins is linked statically.
- The upstream vcpkg triplet builds dependencies (ICU etc.) as dynamic libraries.

dbghelp, shlwapi and winmm are DLLs in System32. synchronization.lib resolves to an API-set DLL (api-ms-win-core-synch-*) that kernelbase backs. So the "system DLLs only" idea is still possible, but the list is wrong as written.

There is also more the reviewer missed:
1. WTF OSAllocatorWin.cpp soft-links kernelbase.dll at runtime (SOFT_LINK_LIBRARY(kernelbase), probably for VirtualAlloc2/MapViewOfFile3). It is a system DLL, but it is loaded dynamically.
2. Upstream WebCore/PlatformWin.cmake adds crypt32, iphlpapi, usp10 and ws2_32. MediaFoundation pulls in d3d9, dwrite, dxva2, evr, mf and mfplat, delay-loaded. The doc's list has no iphlpapi, usp10 or dwrite, and GDIUtilities.cpp soft-links user32.
3. The paired "CRT statica (/MT)" column clashes with upstream. OptionsMSVC.cmake:58 forces CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY MultiThreadedDLL (/MD), because Swift only ships a release-CRT swiftrt.obj. The triplet also uses VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE dynamic, and both OptionsJSCOnly and OptionsWin include OptionsMSVC. So with the stock options you get vcruntime140/ucrtbase DLLs, which are not part of the claim. ZeroG has to override this in its own Options file and use a static vcpkg triplet such as x64-windows-static, or ICU, zlib and other deps come out as DLLs with a dynamic CRT.

None of this can be checked for certain without a build and a dumpbin /dependents run on the final binary. Curl and BoringSSL will also add more system imports (for example crypt32, advapi32 or bcryptprimitives).

claims.claim: Windows: static CRT (/MT)
claims.evidence: OptionsMSVC.cmake:57-58 has `set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY MultiThreadedDLL)` (/MD, also in Debug), justified by 'Swift only ships a release-CRT swiftrt.obj'. x64-windows-webkit.cmake:2,5 sets VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE dynamic and VCPKG_BUILD_TYPE release. webkitdirs.pm:3172 passes -DCMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY=MultiThreadedDLL for cross builds. cmake_minimum_required(3.20) means CMP0091 is NEW, so the variable takes effect.
claims.implication: /MT is possible but needs an override in OptionsZeroG.cmake after include(OptionsMSVC): set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY MultiThreaded). A -D on the command line does not work because the normal variable shadows it. ICU and every other dependency must also be built /MT.

challenge.reasoning:
The reviewer's facts are right, but REFUTED is the wrong verdict. In the "Cosa resta dinamico a runtime" table, "CRT statica (/MT)" is a decision ZeroG is making for its own port. It does not say what upstream does. The checkout does not contradict it. It only shows that upstream's default is /MD, so ZeroG has to override it on purpose.

What the reviewer got right:
- Upstream forces the DLL CRT in every configuration. OptionsMSVC.cmake:58 has `set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY MultiThreadedDLL)`.
- OptionsMSVC is pulled in by OptionsWin.cmake:2 and OptionsJSCOnly.cmake:4.
- The vcpkg triplets use dynamic CRT linkage and release-only builds.
- The top-level CMakeLists.txt requires CMake 3.20, so policy CMP0091 is NEW and the variable takes effect.
- A non-cache `set()` hides a cache value given with -D on the command line, so passing -D alone will not switch to /MT.

What the reviewer missed:
1. The reason upstream gives for /MD does not apply to ZeroG. The comment at OptionsMSVC.cmake:57 is about Swift ("Swift only ships a release-CRT swiftrt.obj"). Swift is only enabled when SWIFT_REQUIRED is on (CMakeLists.txt:32-38). Outside Apple, that only happens when ENABLE_BACK_FORWARD_LIST_SWIFT or ENABLE_IPC_TESTING_SWIFT is on (WebKitFeatures.cmake:577-581). Both are WebKit2/IPC features, and ZeroG has no WebKit2, so it has no Swift and no hard reason to use /MD.
2. ZeroG writes its own OptionsZeroG.cmake, so it does not have to include OptionsMSVC at all. It can include it and then reset the runtime library afterwards, or copy only the MSVC flags it needs.
3. The tree already supports /MT. windows-cross.cmake:30 builds the runtime name from VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE as `MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>$<$<STREQUAL:${VCPKG_CRT_LINKAGE},dynamic>:DLL>`, and lines 86-92 handle a static setting with /MT. Third-party code inside the checkout also uses /MT: Skia's Dawn build script (cmake_utils.py:326), and the CMake files for capstone, abseil and opus, which switch between static and DLL.

So the claim is feasible but takes deliberate work. Upstream assumes /MD, so ZeroG must:
- set `CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY "MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>"` in its own options file, after any include(OptionsMSVC);

challenge.reasoning:
PARTIAL is the right verdict. The doc's claim (ZeroG.md:414 and :518, plus :199) describes a goal: on Linux, only glibc and the GPU drivers stay dynamic, and the drivers are loaded with dlopen. The upstream CMake does not deliver that as it stands. Skia's CMake requires Fontconfig and FreeType on Linux, links libEGL (or epoxy or ANGLE) directly, and always links JPEG and PNG. WebCore's own CMake also links EGL/GLES or epoxy directly, which the reviewer did not mention. Nothing in the tree prevents reaching the goal, though, so the claim cannot be called false.

The reviewer's evidence lines are accurate, but parts of their conclusion are overstated or wrong:
(1) "Add Vulkan, Metal or D3D backends" makes this sound like new work. The bundled Skia tree already contains the backend sources: src/gpu/ganesh/vk (70 files), ganesh/d3d (54), ganesh/mtl (51), graphite/vk (39), graphite/dawn (29), src/gpu/vk (12), src/gpu/mtl, plus include/gpu/vk and include/third_party/vulkan headers. The only missing piece is the CMake wiring. The CMake does already compile SkSLSPIRVCodeGenerator.cpp (line 716).
(2) "Skia must be patched to load EGL through dlopen" is not required. There are two existing paths. With USE_LIBEPOXY and a static libepoxy, Skia goes through epoxy_eglGetProcAddress (GrGLMakeEpoxyEGLInterface.cpp), and libepoxy itself dlopens libEGL, libGL and libGLES at runtime (this is how libepoxy is designed; it cannot be seen in this tree). The other path is the bundled ANGLE: USE_ANGLE_EGL, ANGLE's ANGLE_PLATFORM_LINUX, and ${CMAKE_DL_LIBS}, with ANGLE loading the system GL or Vulkan drivers. Either way, WebCore needs the same choice, because WebCore/CMakeLists.txt:2299-2316 picks ANGLE::EGL+GLES, Epoxy::Epoxy, or OpenGL::GLES + ${EGL_LIBRARIES}.
(3) Fontconfig does not have to be dropped for this claim. It only has to stop being dynamic, which static fontconfig + expat + freetype achieves (fontconfig still reads /etc/fonts at runtime). If ZeroG wants embedded fonts instead, replacements already exist in the tree: src/ports/SkFontMgr_custom_embedded.cpp, SkFontMgr_custom_directory.cpp and SkFontMgr_custom_empty.cpp. Only the CMake source list at lines 845-852 has to change. JPEG and PNG can likewise be linked statically.
(4) The doc's wording "only glibc" also hides a gotcha. On the proposed 2.28 baseline (before glibc 2.34), libpthread.so.0, libdl.so.2, libm.so.6 and librt.so.1 are separate DT_NEEDED shared objects. libstdc++ and libgcc_s must be linked statically with explicit flags, or they become dynamic dependencies too.

challenge.reasoning:
I tried to show the reviewer was wrong and could not. Perl, Python and Ruby are required unconditionally at configure time for every port. gperf is required only when ENABLE_WEBCORE is on, which it is for ZeroG, and WebCore's generators really do call it. That makes four of the five tools in the claim correct.

unifdef is the wrong one. It is never an external host requirement here, and nothing ZeroG builds uses it. Source/CMakeLists.txt either looks for a system unifdef (only when USE_SYSTEM_UNIFDEF is set) or adds the bundled copy in Source/ThirdParty/unifdef. That bundled target is EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL, so it is only compiled if something depends on it. The only CMake users are FindGIDocgen (GLib docs), GLibMacros generate-api-header.py (the GTK/WPE WebKit2 public API headers) and WebKitLegacy/PlatformCocoa.cmake. ZeroG uses none of these, since it has no WebKit2, no GLib API and no Cocoa WebKitLegacy. The postprocess-header-rule scripts in JavaScriptCore/WebKit are only used by the Xcode build, never from CMake. One more point against the doc: the claim says these tools are needed during the build, but Perl, Python and Ruby are hard failures already at configure time.

The reviewer's line numbers are about 5 lines too high (they cite 282-283, 286, 293-325 and 352-358; the actual lines are 277-278, 281, 288-318 and 366-371). The substance is unchanged.

Things the doc misses for implementation:
(a) A ZeroG OptionsZeroG.cmake does not need to define USE_SYSTEM_UNIFDEF. If it is left undefined the bundled unifdef directory is added but never built, which is harmless. Only GTK and WPE set it ON; JSCOnly sets it OFF.

(c) On WIN32, $SystemDrive/cygwin/bin is added to the program search path, so a Cygwin gperf or perl can be picked up there.
(d) The Ruby check is a hand-written find_program on `ruby` plus a version query. It can be pinned with -DRUBY_EXECUTABLE or -DRuby_EXECUTABLE.
(e) The 3.0.1 gperf minimum is passed to find_package, but there is a 'TODO Enforce version requirement' comment, so it may not be strictly enforced.
(f) Python 3 is mandatory. WebCore's CSS property/value/pseudo-selector generators and the HTTP header-name table generator run Python and pass gperf through to it.

I tried to show the reviewer was wrong and couldn't. Every piece of their evidence checks out, and I found more. The doc (ZeroG.md:527) says step 2 adds WebCore with "only Skia, HarfBuzz, FreeType, libxml2 and SQLite". Step 3 (ZeroG.md:528) then defers images (libpng, libjpeg-turbo, libwebp) to later. 2) Skia.cmake requires HarfBuzz::ICU, and the Skia text shaper calls hb_icu_script_to_script. That contradicts both "HarfBuzz without ICU" in the dependency table (ZeroG.md:460) and the step-2 list.

4) The image-decoder dependencies cannot be put off until a later step. Generic ImageDecoder.cpp (in Sources.txt) always includes ScalableImageDecoder and calls it. ScalableImageDecoder.cpp includes the JPEG/PNG/WebP decoders on every non-Cocoa platform, and those include <jpeglib.h> and <png.h>. ImageDecoders.cmake links JPEG::JPEG, PNG::PNG and WebP::demux, and every CMake Platform*.cmake (GTK, WPE, Win, PlayStation, Haiku) includes it. Platform macros: without a BUILDING_<X>__ define, PlatformLegacy.h:48-77 sets PLATFORM(WIN) on Windows and PLATFORM(MAC)/PLATFORM(COCOA) on macOS, and BPlatform.h:121-129 sets BPLATFORM_WIN. JSCOnly avoids this with -DBUILDING_JSCONLY__ (OptionsJSCOnly.cmake:11), which deliberately provides no PLATFORM() at all. PlayStation uses -DWTF_PLATFORM_PLAYSTATION=1 plus PlatformEnablePlayStation.h (PlatformEnable.h:122-124). ZeroG needs a header patch adding BUILDING_ZEROG__ / WTF_PLATFORM_ZEROG, and probably a PlatformEnableZeroG.h.

WEBKIT_OPTION_BEGIN() is where every ENABLE_*/USE_* option is defined (WebKitFeatures.cmake:96-398). OptionsZeroG.cmake must call WEBKIT_OPTION_BEGIN/END and set defaults with WEBKIT_OPTION_DEFAULT_PORT_VALUE. PRIVATE options are only mark_as_advanced and can still be set with -D (WebKitFeatures.cmake:524-527). A plain set() after WEBKIT_OPTION_END overrides user -D values; JSCOnly does this for ENABLE_API_TESTS.

PAL needs its own PlatformZeroG.cmake in Source/WebCore/PAL/pal/, which the doc omits. PlayStation's version adds crypto/openssl/CryptoDigestOpenSSL.cpp, system/ClockGeneric.cpp, system/Sound.cpp and text/KillRing.cpp and links OpenSSL::Crypto, so BoringSSL is needed already at the PAL level.

Windows: USE_SYSTEM_MALLOC=ON is a hard #error ('System malloc configuration is not supported in Windows since aligned memory cannot be freed via ::free. Use mimalloc instead', bmalloc/bmalloc/BPlatform.h:431-433). libpas is enabled on Windows/Linux x86_64/arm64/Darwin (BPlatform.h:400).

Windows final link requirements set by OptionsMSVC.cmake, which an external zig/lld-link step must replicate: clang_rt.builtins-x86_64.lib (:128-141, found under <clang-cl>/../lib/clang/<major>/lib/windows, REQUIRED), /OPT:NOICF /OPT:REF /DEBUG (:83, ICF is unsafe for WebKit), /STACK:8388608 (:143), /INCREMENTAL:NO, and AT&T inline asm (/clang:-masm=att).

The upstream Windows flow (build-webkit/build-jsc) uses vcpkg manifest mode: root vcpkg.json depends on icu, vcpkg-configuration.json pins microsoft/vcpkg plus the WebKitForWindows/WebKitRequirements registry for icu, curl, openssl, zlib and others, and the overlay triplet WebKitLibraries/triplets/x64-windows-webkit.cmake is dynamic CRT, dynamic libs, release only. The 'web' feature uses libressl (curl[libressl]) rather than BoringSSL (vcpkg.json).

On clang (non-MSVC) with precompiled headers enabled, the JIT/DFG/FTL/bytecode/llint objects (JavaScriptCoreJIT) and the WebCore JSBindings/Style/DOMAndRendering/Inspector objects are not stored in libJavaScriptCore.a or libWebCore.a. They are only INTERFACE link items (WebKitMacros.cmake:409-437). Linux thin archives are on by default (OptionsCommon.cmake:167-182). Both break 'collect the archives and link with zig'; use -DUSE_THIN_ARCHIVES=OFF -DCMAKE_DISABLE_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS=ON or harvest the object lists.

The doc says zig does the final link. Zig links its bundled LLVM libc++ by default, while clang on Linux compiles WebKit against the system libstdc++, and clang-cl compiles against the MSVC STL. Mixing them breaks the C++ ABI. Either compile WebKit with the same stdlib/toolchain as the final link (e.g. CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER='zig c++') or have zig only link C objects and let a clang/lld step carry the C++ runtime. This is inferred from toolchain behaviour and needs a test build.

Bundled Skia (Source/ThirdParty/skia/CMakeLists.txt) has a Windows branch using the DirectWrite font manager (:814-826), and its non-Windows branch is FreeType+Fontconfig (:827-854) with no CoreText/macOS branch. The only GPU backend is Ganesh GL via EGL or epoxy (:856-867), with no Vulkan, Metal or D3D sources. Skia is add_library(Skia STATIC) (:21).
WebCore's Skia path requires HarfBuzz built with ICU: Skia.cmake:37-41 links HarfBuzz::ICU and ComplexTextControllerSkia.cpp:35 includes <hb-icu.h>. This contradicts the doc's 'HarfBuzz without ICU'.

There is a MinGW path in WebKitCompilerFlags.cmake:211-215 (-mno-ms-bitfields, __USE_MINGW_ANSI_STDIO) for WIN32 without clang-cl, and OptionsJSCOnly only includes OptionsMSVC when MSVC is set. It is not exercised by build scripts or CI, so clang-cl remains the only supported Windows toolchain.

Source/WTF/wtf, WebCore and PAL contain orphan PlatformHaiku.cmake files and PlatformLegacy.h has a BUILDING_HAIKU__ branch, but there is no OptionsHaiku.cmake and Haiku is not in ALL_PORTS. It is a small reference for adding a new PLATFORM() macro.

challenge.reasoning:
This claim is about Ultralight's licensing, which is outside the WebKit checkout, so I checked it against Ultralight's own pages. All three parts hold.

1. **"DLL" and "no static linking under the free license."** LICENSE.txt section 4.2 forbids accessing Ultralight.dll "using static-linking tools", unless otherwise agreed in writing. Section 1.1.3 says the software ships as static libraries, dynamically-linked libraries and documentation.

2. **"Core proprietary, WebCore LGPL/BSD."** The GitHub README table lists UltralightCore and Ultralight as Proprietary, WebCore as LGPL/BSD and AppCore as LGPL.

3. **Where the reviewer went wrong.** They downgraded the claim to PARTIAL, saying the ban covers "every license unless agreed in writing, not only the free one". That misreads the document. LICENSE.txt is the free license itself: section 6.1 calls it "this Free License Agreement" and says no payment or royalty is required. For commercial use or extra rights it says to contact Ultralight Inc. Paid licenses (Indie, Pro, Enterprise) are separate agreements that are not public. So section 4.2 only proves the ban for the free license, which is exactly what the doc says. Whether paid contracts also ban static linking cannot be checked publicly. The fact that Enterprise includes source access makes a blanket ban across all tiers less likely. The doc's wording is the precise one.

The reviewer's side notes are accurate. The pricing page lists a 60 FPS cap, no JS JIT and no media playback for the Free SDK. It sets the free limit at under $200K turnover and funding, while the README and LICENSE.txt section 2.3 still say $100K. Source access is Enterprise only. These could be added to the comparison table, but they don't make the existing claim wrong.

Missing context for ZeroG: Ultralight is split into several libraries (UltralightCore, WebCore, Ultralight, AppCore), not one DLL. Ultralight's LGPL WebCore fork is the part that can legally be studied and reused. Under the doc's per-file license tracking rule (line 557), any code ZeroG takes from it is LGPL.

claims.claim: oven-sh/WebKit PR 235 moved the GC signal default from SIGUSR1 to SIGPWR and fixed the GC hang with a host alternate signal stack
claims.evidence: PR 235 ('WTF: read interrupted SP from ucontext in signalHandlerSuspendResume', opened 2026-05-21) is still OPEN and was never merged. It changes only Source/WTF/wtf/posix/ThreadingPOSIX.cpp (+68/-10). It does not change the default signal. The SIGPWR default came from oven-sh/WebKit commit ceb3e7466fa4 (2025-02-07, 'Change default suspend/resume signal from SIGUSR1 to SIGPWR for Bun'), behind '#if USE(BUN_JSC_ADDITIONS)', with a comment citing npm packages that use SIGUSR1 and noting that Mono's GC also uses SIGPWR. The alt-stack fix was merged as PR 817 (merge d6375c72, 2026-10-21; 'This is #235 rebased on main (#693 changed the handler)'). A related fix, PR 693 (merge ddd87b08, 2026-09-20), makes the handler act only on requests from suspend()/resume(), so a stray SIGPWR no longer segfaults at ThreadingPOSIX.cpp:140. Mechanism: Go's runtime.setsigstack adds SA_ONSTACK to foreign handlers; the handler checks currentStackPointer() (its own frame, on the alt stack) against m_stack, fails on every try, and Thread::suspend() spins forever. Open follow-ups: PR 742 (alt stacks for WTF threads), PR 794.
claims.implication: Re-cite as commit ceb3e74 (SIGPWR) + PR 693 + PR 817 (fixes). Upstream main still has both bugs: ThreadingPOSIX.cpp:138-140 dereferences targetThread unconditionally, and lines 150-161 use currentStackPointer(). ZeroG must carry PR 693 and PR 817 in patches/ (or upstream them) before the doc's CI 'crash handler + alt stack' test can pass. A host using Go c-shared libs, ASan or Breakpad/Crashpad would otherwise hang the GC.

challenge.reasoning:
I tried to prove the reviewer wrong and could not. Every point they made checks out against GitHub (via gh) and the local checkout.

1. PR 235 did not change the default signal. It is still OPEN (created 2026-05-21, never merged or closed) and touches only Source/WTF/wtf/posix/ThreadingPOSIX.cpp (+68/-10). Its body treats SIGPWR as already the default ("Fixes the SIGPWR suspend-loop deadlock reported in oven-sh/bun#31158"). It does not introduce SIGPWR.

2. The SIGUSR1 to SIGPWR move is commit ceb3e7466fa43aae8cf2c75353c59bd821f03d06 (2025-02-07), titled "Change default suspend/resume signal from SIGUSR1 to SIGPWR for Bun". It sits behind #if USE(BUN_JSC_ADDITIONS), and its comment cites npm packages that use SIGUSR1 and notes that Mono's GC also uses SIGPWR. So the doc is wrong to say both changes came from "the same work" ("Nello stesso lavoro"). The signal change came about 15 months before the alt-stack fix, in a separate commit.

3. The alt-stack hang fix did land, but as PR 817 (MERGED 2026-10-21, merge d6375c72affe0f70222cdcb45012b10f0bf3a9d5). Its body says "This is #235 rebased on main (#693 changed the handler)". PR 693 (MERGED 2026-09-20, merge ddd87b080df3ba77ffb82d79383df81ea2970216) is "[WTF] The thread suspend signal handler acts only on requests from suspend() and resume()".

The substance of the claim is true: Bun moved to SIGPWR because npm packages use SIGUSR1, and Bun fixed a GC hang caused by alternate signal stacks (ASan, crash handlers, Go c-shared via runtime.setsigstack). The attribution to PR 235 and the "same work" framing are wrong. That makes PARTIAL correct, not CONFIRMED and not fully REFUTED.

The reviewer's implication also holds for the pinned upstream checkout:
- ThreadingPOSIX.cpp:198 still defaults to SIGUSR1, with the JSC_SIGNAL_FOR_GC override at 199-205.
- Lines 138-140 load targetThread and dereference thread->m_suspendCount with no null check. A stray suspend signal while targetThread is null (the case PR 693 fixes) is a null dereference.
- Line 150 uses currentStackPointer() for the m_stack check (151-161). On an alt stack this check fails on every retry (the case PR 817 fixes).

Doc corrections:
- Cite commit ceb3e74 for the signal change, and PR 693 + PR 817 for the fixes (PR 235 only as the original, unmerged attempt).
- Drop "Nello stesso lavoro".

Implementation notes:
- ZeroG's own signal choice must not depend on BUN_JSC_ADDITIONS. Set g_wtfConfig.sigThreadSuspendResume and isUserSpecifiedThreadSuspendResumeSignalConfigured before WTF initializes, or patch the default.
- Carry PR 693 + PR 817 in patches/ until upstream has equivalents.

A programmatic API exists: JSConfigureSignalForGC(int) in Source/JavaScriptCore/API/JSBasePrivate.h:58, implemented in JSBase.cpp:185-193 under '#if !OS(DARWIN) && !OS(WINDOWS)'. It returns false if called after initializePlatformThreading has run.
claims.implication: The current behaviour is worse than a crash: the host's SIGUSR1 handler is silently replaced. zg_runtime_config can map directly to JSConfigureSignalForGC, which must run before WTF::initializeMainThread / JSC::initialize. A real-time default must be computed at runtime (SIGRTMIN+n; glibc reserves the lowest RT signals). Avoid SIGPWR as ZeroG's default, because Mono and Boehm GC use it.

challenge.reasoning:
I tried to prove the reviewer wrong and could not. The claim has three parts, and the checkout confirms two of them.

1. The default is SIGUSR1: confirmed.
2. It can be changed with the JSC_SIGNAL_FOR_GC environment variable: confirmed. The variable was not renamed or removed.
3. WebKit checks that nobody else handles the signal, and a host that already uses it (Ruby) crashes: out of date. The code still checks whether a handler is already installed. If it finds one, it only logs a warning (WTFLogAlways), then installs its own handler in place of the host's without calling it. The RELEASE_ASSERT on line 237 only fires if sigaction() itself fails, not when the signal is already taken. Bugzilla 223069 confirms the abort was removed in r275014 (2021-03-25) and replaced with the "Overriding existing handler" log. The doc's source describes the behaviour from before that fix.

The reviewer's other points also hold:
- JSConfigureSignalForGC(int) exists, declared in JSBasePrivate.h and implemented in JSBase.cpp. It returns false once isThreadSuspendResumeSignalConfigured is set, which happens in Thread::initializePlatformThreading. So it must be called before WTF/JSC initialization.
- Its exact guard is `!OS(DARWIN) && !OS(WINDOWS)` in the .cpp and `!__APPLE__ && !WIN32` in the header. It is a private header (JSBasePrivate.h), so ZeroG must install or include it explicitly.

Small corrections and additions to the doc:
- The problem is not limited to Linux. The handler-install code is guarded by `!OS(DARWIN)`, so it also applies to FreeBSD and other non-Darwin POSIX systems. Darwin still assigns SIGUSR1 to the config field but installs no handler.
- The opposite order is also a problem. If the host installs its own SIGUSR1 handler after JSC has started, it replaces JSC's handler. JSC does not detect this. The likely result is that GC thread suspension hangs (the handler posts a semaphore and calls sigsuspend), not a clean crash. This is an inference from the code, not something I tested.
- Threads not created by WTF must be registered through initializeCurrentThreadEvenIfNonWTFCreated, which unblocks the signal. A host that blocks the GC signal in its own threads' signal masks will interfere with this.
- The doc's proposal is right that the signal should be chosen in zg_runtime_config; it can map directly onto JSConfigureSignalForGC. The real-time signal number must be picked at runtime, as SIGRTMIN+n.
