challenge.reasoning:
I tried to prove the reviewer wrong and could not. The mechanism they describe is right. Thread suspension for the GC uses Mach thread_suspend on Darwin and SuspendThread on Windows. On every other POSIX target it uses a signal, chosen in initializePlatformThreading. That code is guarded by `#if !OS(DARWIN)`, not by OS(LINUX), so it runs on any OS(UNIX) system that is not Darwin: Linux, Android, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, Haiku, QNX, Hurd, Fuchsia and PlayStation. The CMake files back this up: ThreadingPOSIX.cpp is compiled for GTK, WPE, JSCOnly, PlayStation, Haiku and Cocoa, while ThreadingWin.cpp is compiled for Win and JSCOnly on Windows. So the claim "Linux-only" is too narrow. The accurate wording is "every non-Darwin POSIX target". For ZeroG's targets (Windows, macOS, Linux), Linux is the only desktop platform affected, which is why I rate it PARTIAL and not REFUTED.

The claim also breaks down for the second half of the doc section, which covers SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGILL trap handlers. That problem is not Linux-only either; each platform just uses a different mechanism:
- macOS: JSC handles traps through Mach exception ports. This is enabled by HAVE(MACH_EXCEPTIONS) plus Options::useMachForExceptions. Host crash handlers on macOS, such as Crashpad, also use Mach exception ports, so they can conflict with JSC.
- Darwin, Signal::Usr: this one still goes through POSIX sigaction even when Mach is enabled.
- Windows: SignalsWin.cpp installs a first-in-line vectored exception handler with AddVectoredExceptionHandler(1, ...). That changes the order in which the host's own handlers run.
So the doc's point that JSC's handlers must chain with the host's applies on all three platforms.

Points the doc misses:
1. An official API already exists: JSConfigureSignalForGC(int) in JSBase.cpp. It is compiled only for non-Darwin, non-Windows builds. It returns false once the signal has been configured, so it must be called before WTF threading initializes. The doc's proposal (choose the signal in zg_runtime_config instead of an environment variable) can be built directly on it; no patch is needed.
2. Even with the API, the JSC_SIGNAL_FOR_GC environment variable is still read when no user signal has been set.
3. If another handler is already installed on that signal, WebKit only logs a warning ("Overriding existing handler") and replaces it; the GC itself does not crash at that point. The crash comes later, when the host's own use of that signal reaches JSC's handler.
4. Upstream already has the alternate-signal-stack back-off described in the doc (the m_stack.contains check, which posts the semaphore and retries).
5. HAVE_MACH_EXCEPTIONS is turned off when PLATFORM(GTK) is set. A new ZeroG port on macOS must not define PLATFORM(GTK), or it will fall back to POSIX signals for traps.

challenge.reasoning:
I tried to prove the reviewer wrong and could not. The claim (ZeroG.md:82, and the same idea at :69) treats both ports as one group: "CMake without GLib, RunLoopGeneric, curl networking, Skia planned". It is only accurate when split by port:

JSCOnly has no Skia because it has no WebCore.
- One small slip in the reviewer's evidence: they cite the ENABLE_STATIC_JSC line ":19" without naming the file. That line is in OptionsJSCOnly.cmake, and it defaults to PUBLIC OFF. PlayStation defaults it to ON at OptionsPlayStation.cmake:173.

(c) PlayStation sets USE_SKIA_ENCODERS OFF (:232).
(d) PlayStation needs curl 7.85.0 or newer (:105).

missing_facts: Upstream main (checkout 31a83a39) still has both GC suspend-signal bugs Bun fixed. Source/WTF/wtf/posix/ThreadingPOSIX.cpp:138-140 dereferences targetThread on any delivery, so a stray signal (kill -USR1) segfaults. Lines 150-161 compare currentStackPointer() with m_stack, so the suspender spins forever if any library adds SA_ONSTACK (Go cgo runtime.setsigstack, Mono, JNI) while an alt stack is installed (ASan, Crashpad). Fixes: oven-sh/WebKit PR 693 (merge ddd87b080df3, 2026-09-20) and PR 817 (merge d6375c72affe, 2026-10-21), both touching only ThreadingPOSIX.cpp.
ThreadingPOSIX.cpp:231-233 silently overrides an existing host handler for the GC signal and only logs it (WTFLogAlways). There is no chaining, so the host loses its handler without crashing.

JSConfigureSignalForGC(int) already exists (Source/JavaScriptCore/API/JSBasePrivate.h:58, JSBase.cpp:185-193). It is a private header, unavailable on Darwin/Windows, and must be called before WTF platform threading init (it returns false afterwards). zg_runtime_config should wrap it.

Don't pick SIGPWR as ZeroG's default: Bun's own commit comment notes Mono's GC uses SIGPWR, and Boehm GC uses it on Linux too. Compute real-time signals at runtime (SIGRTMIN+n); glibc reserves the lowest RT signals.

WTF/wtf/threads/Signals.cpp:590 installs trap handlers with sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO and no SA_ONSTACK, so a stack overflow on a WTF thread dies silently (oven-sh PR 742, still open). Chaining (:528-541) works only for handlers installed before JSC.
